The distinction only remains meaningful if the checklist is claimed to encode causal structure, in which case adversarial items that break surface-to-structure mappings within a single evaluation distinguish faithful causal execution from blind proxy-tracking.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist is explicitly causal but the evaluation distribution happens to preserve surface-to-structure alignment on all items including adversarial ones, making the single evaluation unable to distinguish compliance from genuine reasoning without cross-distribution evidence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel's reliability gain is driven by Condorcet-style aggregation of independent errors rather than by faithful execution of the frozen theory, meaning the checklist-vs-causal-reasoning frame misidentifies the actual source of the gain.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's internal theory is demonstrably superior to the frozen checklist theory on the evaluated distribution (e.g., novel domain edge cases), so the panel's checklist compliance produces worse outcomes than expert intuition despite higher consistency.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A checklist functions as a 'frozen theory' encoding its author's causal model in procedural form. Non-expert panelists execute this frozen theory faithfully; experts execute their own mutable, potentially-biased internal theory. If the checklist is explicitly a surface heuristic (no causal claim), then compliance IS the mechanism of reliability, and the distinction between genuine gain and mere compliance-tracking is moot. If the checklist claims to capture causal structure, the distinction becomes meaningful, and adversarial items\u2014where surface features correlate with the wrong outcome while structural features indicate the correct outcome\u2014test whether panelists follow causal structure or merely surface proxies. Distinguishing genuine gain from compliance-tracking thus requires first classifying the checklist's epistemic status (causal vs. correlational), then applying adversarial probes only in the causal case.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
